result.title: Action-Conditioned VLM Monitoring for Autonomous Vehicle Semantic Anomalies
result.summary: We study action-conditioned monitoring of autonomous-vehicle behavior in semantically unusual driving scenes. The target is whether the executed ego action is appropriate for the scene: the same scene can admit both normal and anomalous behavior, so visual unusualness alone does not determine the monitoring label. A Vision-Language Model (VLM) first predicts the scene-required action from an outcome-hidden video window; the monitor then compares that expectation with the realized ego-motion trajectory under an explicit compatibility rule. To study this monitoring task, we contribute a six-field taxonomy of 112 paired scenarios spanning both failure polarities (42 derived from documented incidents), a generated video corpus with estimated trajectories, and an exploratory two-stage monitor on that corpus. On 235 clips from 15 scenario families, the two-stage protocol with a fixed T-2.5 s window obtains 83.0% accuracy and anomaly recall 0.773, versus 74.5% and 0.536 for a single-stage video-only baseline; specificity is 0.880 versus 0.928.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究自动驾驶中的「动作条件化」语义异常监控：VLM 先从结果隐藏的视频窗口预测场景所要求的动作，再与真实自车轨迹按显式兼容规则比对；同时给出 112 个配对场景的六字段分类体系与视频语料，两阶段协议取得 83.0% 准确率、异常召回 0.773（单阶段视频基线为 74.5%/0.536，但特异度下降）。
AI.relevance_reason: 以「场景应有动作」作显式中间表示再与观测行为核验，可供核查 VLM 视觉理解是否真正进入判定、以及该中间假设在召回与特异度上的代价，与 LVR 中视觉证据使用和评价设计有具体联系。
